paras: Phrynocephalus forsythii, also known commonly as Forsyth's toadhead agama and Forsyth's toad-headed lizard, is a species of lizard in the family Agamidae. The species is endemic to China.
The specific name, forsythii, is in honor of English diplomat Thomas Douglas Forsyth.
P. forsythii is found in northwestern China, in the Tarim Basin portion of the autonomous region of Xinjiang.
The preferred natural habitat of P. forsythii is desert, at altitudes of 887–3,200 m (2,910–10,499 ft).
P. forsythii is ovoviviparous. Litter size is one to six young.
